Rewrote the Shared live surface section against surface-hub.ts (bounded per-viewer H.264 queue of 32 units or 4 MiB, keyframe-only start, overflow resync, keyframe requests at most every 500 ms, codec demand), device-live-surface-producer.ts (passthrough with parameter sets prepended, fitted header size, ffmpeg only for image viewers), routes/live-surface.ts (?codec=h264), useLiveSurface.ts and liveSurfaceStreamAdmission.ts (two frame streams per origin, queued status, 400 fallback), liveSurfaceVideoDecoder.ts and the canvas codec line. Evidence names the two real-browser suites. The multiplexed stream remains documented as not built.

Added the 2026-11-02 amendment: per-origin cap of two frame streams with the measured real-browser HTTP/1.1 result (baseline tap not received in 2 s; capped p50 1 ms, p95 2 ms, lease 1 ms) bound to revision 9a0c060aa1, Apple M5 Pro, macOS 26.7.2, Chromium 156. States the open case (all three view-scoped streams), the unbuilt multiplexed stream, and unqualified native and relay transports. Updated the reading-status paragraph to match.

Qualified latest-frame-wins as image-only in the fan-out and relay paragraphs, and added the interim per-pane streams with the admission cap and the bounded H.264 queue with keyframe resync, against surface-hub.ts and liveSurfaceStreamAdmission.ts.

Updated Android video against device-live-surface-producer.ts and the canvas: H.264 decoded in a capable browser (secure context, WebCodecs, profile accepted) with the pane's codec line, server ffmpeg only while an image viewer is open, PNG polling otherwise. Live emulator behavior was not run (NOT_VERIFIED in the PR).

Replaced the unqualified transport paragraph with the two-per-origin cap, the visible waiting state and the HTTP/1.1 measurement reference; native, relay and the multiplexed stream remain stated as not qualified or not built.

Re-read the Browser pane, live surface and control lease entries against the changed contract and hub; the definitions (one producer fanned out to viewers, typed input, lease) remain accurate with H.264 viewers and admission. No claims changed.
Updated the live-surface row for the h264 codec, the keyframe header flag and parseLiveSurfaceH264Sequence, checked against packages/contracts/src/live-surface.ts and its tests.

Checked the README's description of pure parsers against the new SPS reader and keyframe header validation in live-surface.ts; both are pure, environment-free parsers, so the README stays accurate. No claims changed.

Updated the live-frames finding: the admission cap now reserves connections for input and was measured in a real browser over HTTP/1.1; the shared cross-surface transport and the three-view-scoped-stream case remain open under #2760.
